Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
35-year-old male with 3–6 month history of reduced appetite, fatigue, mild weight loss, episodic palpitations/subjective dyspnoea in lifts, and nausea; underactive thyroid off thyroxine; blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: ↓ appetite and energy for ~3.5 months, coinciding with new job.  
• Associated symptoms:  
  – Weight loss <1 stone (~6 kg) over ~6 months.  
  – Nausea intermittently; no vomiting.  
  – Episodic palpitations and feeling short of breath mainly in elevators; no limitation walking “about a mile” but later states not walking recently.  
  – Headaches, low mood/“feeling down.”  
• Pertinent negatives: no chest pain, no cough, no diarrhoea, no blood or mucus in stool, no reflux.  
• Past medical history: Hypothyroidism (previously on thyroxine).  
• Medications: Thyroxine (dose/route/frequency not documented) – patient stopped “since changed doctor.”  
• Allergies: not discussed.  
• Social / preventive: Works as lawyer; married. No other social history provided.

Examination:
• Vitals: not recorded.  
• Physical exam: not performed (virtual consult).

Impression:
Unexplained fatigue, anorexia, mild weight loss, and palpitations; differential includes anaemia, thyroid dysfunction (due to stopped thyroxine), nutritional deficiency, or other systemic illness.

Plan:
• Order comprehensive blood panel: FBC, U&E, LFT, TFT, vitamin levels, ± others per local protocol.  
• Arrange blood draw via support line; patient instructed to call number provided.  
• Follow-up: patient will receive text to book review once results available.  
• Safety-netting: Attend A&E for chest pain or severe palpitations; re-contact service for vomiting or bowel habit change.  
• Physical examination to be arranged if bloods non-diagnostic or symptoms progress.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: allergies, current medication list (other than thyroxine), substance use, family history, vitals, mental health screen.  
● Internal conflicts: patient states able to walk a mile without breathlessness yet later reports not walking lately—conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: clear overall; occasional interruptions and minor inaudible phrases but key clinical details audible.
